summary: A stand-in page for old addresses. It sends visitors straight to the new address and shows a short notice with a link.
purpose: Keeps old links working on a static site.
why: The file comment says it handles legacy routes in the static export. A static site cannot run server redirects, so the move happens in the browser.
how: Once the page loads, it replaces the current address with the target address. It also shows the sentence that the page has moved, with a link to the new address.
inputs: The target address and the link label.
outputs: A page with a notice and a link, and a browser move to the target address.
risks: The move only happens after JavaScript runs. Visitors with scripts turned off see only the notice. Search engines may not follow the move.
debug: If an old link stays on the notice, check that the target path exists and that JavaScript loads on the page.
